frozen_original.title: Intelligence Decapitation: Trump Purges NSA, Cyber Command, and IC Leadership on Loomer's Orders
frozen_original.synopsis: In April 2025, President Trump fired Gen. Timothy Haugh, the four-star director of the National Security Agency and head of U.S. Cyber Command, along with his deputy Wendy Noble — at the explicit urging of MAGA activist Laura Loomer, who had flagged them on social media as disloyal. NSA and Cyber Command director positions remained vacant for months, during a period when Trump's own intelligence officials were publicly warning of escalating Chinese and Russian cyberattacks. By November 2025, Senator Mark Warner warned of catastrophic consequences, noting CISA had lost one-third of its workforce, the FBI's top cyber official had been fired, and NSA/Cyber Command leadership remained empty. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard followed with an August 2025 memo revoking the security clearances of 37 career professionals — including the CIA's top Russia analyst, a 29-year veteran — effective immediately upon her return from helping brief Trump on the Alaska-Putin summit. Former CIA Director William Burns accused the administration of a campaign of retribution masquerading as reform, warning that remaining officials would self-censor rather than risk becoming the next casualty.

primary.split_rationale: The original card combines the April Haugh/Noble personnel action with Gabbard’s distinct August clearance revocation and incorrectly attributes both to Loomer. Two discrete, source-supported event drafts are supplied.

children.title: Trump Dismisses NSA and Cyber Command Chief Timothy Haugh
children.description_short: Trump Dismisses NSA and Cyber Command Chief Timothy Haugh
children.description_medium: On April 3, 2025, President Donald Trump dismissed Gen. Timothy Haugh as director of the National Security Agency and head of U.S. Cyber Command. NSA deputy Wendy Noble was also removed and reassigned. Reuters reported that Laura Loomer had urged Trump to dismiss Haugh and met with him the day before; officials cited in the reporting did not know the reason for the personnel decisions.
children.description_long: On April 3, 2025, President Donald Trump dismissed Gen. Timothy Haugh as director of the National Security Agency and head of U.S. Cyber Command. NSA deputy director Wendy Noble was also removed from her post and reassigned within the Pentagon, according to Reuters. Reuters reported that Laura Loomer, an outside political activist, had urged Trump to dismiss Haugh and met with the president the day before the firing. The reporting does not establish that Loomer had formal authority over the personnel decision, and it does not confirm her accusation that Haugh was disloyal. Officials cited in the reporting said they did not know the reason for Haugh’s dismissal or Noble’s reassignment. The event documented here is the removal of senior leaders from the NSA and Cyber Command; Reuters also situated it within a broader round of White House national-security dismissals. This record does not claim that Loomer ordered the removals or that they caused a specific intelligence failure. It treats the later revocation of 37 intelligence clearances in August as a separate event because the sources describe a different date and decision process.

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends All Federal Family Planning Programs
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, the Trump administration terminated all federal Title X family planning grants — the only dedicated federal program funding contraceptive services, STI testing, and reproductive health counseling for low-income individuals — and eliminated all other federal family planning program funding. Title X had served approximately 4 million patients annually at clinics across all 50 states, providing services including birth control, cancer screenings, and STI treatment. Over 1,600 health centers that depended on Title X funding were forced to reduce services or close. The termination disproportionately affected low-income women, women of color, rural residents, and people without health insurance. Public health researchers projected that the elimination of family planning funding would lead to an increase in unintended pregnancies, maternal mortality, and unsafe abortions.
